title: HIV / ART — WHO baseline (draft)
summary: WHO consolidated HIV guidelines baseline for primary care: test-and-treat, preferred first-line ART, monitoring, prophylaxis and prevention. National programmes (e.g. NASCOP in Kenya) refine drug choices and monitoring cadence — authored as national overlays. DRAFT — clinician verification required before approval.
diagnosis: Diagnose with a validated national HIV testing algorithm (serial rapid tests); confirm before ART start.
Assess for TB, cryptococcal disease (CrAg where CD4 low), and other opportunistic infections at diagnosis.
treatment: Test and treat: offer ART to all people living with HIV regardless of CD4 count or clinical stage.
Rapid ART initiation (same day where the person is ready), once danger conditions excluded.
Preferred first-line (adults & adolescents): TDF + 3TC (or FTC) + DTG (the 'TLD' regimen).
Dolutegravir-based regimens preferred as anchor drug for most populations.
Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis where indicated; TB preventive treatment where eligible.
monitoring: Viral load is the preferred monitoring test: at 6 and 12 months, then annually if suppressed.
Viral suppression target <1000 copies/mL (aim undetectable); investigate and support adherence if not suppressed.
Baseline CD4 to assess advanced HIV disease and OI risk.
prevention: PrEP for people at substantial risk of HIV.
PEP started as soon as possible, within 72 hours of exposure, for 28 days.
PMTCT: lifelong ART for all pregnant and breastfeeding women living with HIV.
redFlags: Advanced HIV disease (CD4 <200) with new headache/fever/neurology — assess for cryptococcal/TB meningitis and refer.
Suspected immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome after ART start.
nationalOverlayNotes: Per-country overlays should adopt the national ART guideline (regimens, paediatric dosing, monitoring intervals) and EML.

references.label: WHO Consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery and monitoring, 2021
